blocking.title: Recall by violation source is missing for the ensemble and the cascade, and the omitted split changes the headline
blocking.evidence: prereg/0003 (Analysis) preregisters 'Breakdowns (descriptive, primary set, headline method): recall by violation source (natural, inserted), by violation type, and by subject model' with no restriction to base monitors, and brief section 5 requires that natural, inserted, and dataset violations are reported separately, including recall by source. tools/analyze.py:461 skips every monitor whose family is not rule or model, so artifacts/e2/results.json has 63 breakdown rows for the 7 base monitors and none for the ensemble or the cascade, which are the only monitors above chance. No deviation is reported. I recomputed the preregistered breakdown with the analysis's own functions and seed rule (analyze.derived_scores, recall_at_budget with the composite method, stable_seed(20261104, monitor id, 'violation_source', value), 2000 resamples) at prevalence 1e-3 and 20 per 10,000. Results: ensemble recall on inserted (synthetic) violations 0.107 [0.064, 0.154] but on natural violations 0.014 [0.003, 0.046]. Cascade recall on inserted 0.032 [0.011, 0.054], on natural 0.014 [0.001, 0.039]. So the first-screen finding (ensemble 0.069 [0.042, 0.102]) comes mostly from synthetic inserted violations. Also, README.md:67-71 says 'Only the two preregistered combinations clear chance', which does not hold for the cascade on natural violations: its interval contains the random-review rate 0.002.

blocking.title: Time to detection for model:qwen3-0.6b-q8_0 counts violations the budget does not catch, but the report says the opposite
blocking.evidence: ttd() counts a violation as caught when any prefix score reaches the full-trace budget threshold. Benign prefixes were never scored, so flagging at the prefix level has no budget. For the 0.6B monitor at 1e-3 and 20 per 10,000, the threshold is 0.2080 (tie fraction 0.748). Only 1 of 1,045 violations has a full-trace score at or above it (recall at budget 0.001). But 127 have some prefix at or above it, and for 126 of those the prefix is the only thing that reaches it (recomputed from artifacts/scores/primary/model_qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.jsonl.gz with baserate.estimate.budget_point). So the REPORT row 'share caught by the end 0.122; at the violating step 0.032 [0.022, 0.043]; median delay 1.000 [1.000, 1.000]' is not what docs/REPORT.md:480-481 says it is ('defined for the violations a monitor catches within the budget'). The sentence 'the few caught violations give wide intervals' is also false for this row (127 caught, interval [1, 1]). prereg/0003 defines time to detection 'for violations caught at that budget', and the REPORT itself reads it that way. Under that reading, the row would show a share caught of 0.001. The deviation is not reported.

blocking.title: E3 prose says recall is near zero in every domain, which the banked E3 pairs contradict for the rule monitor
blocking.evidence: At the E3 setting (full set without Armour violations, prevalence 1e-3, 100 per 10,000), I computed the reviewer-calibrated rule's own-domain recall with budget_point, the same way tools/analyze.py run_e3 computes own0. It is 0.213 in browser and 0.255 in devops (0.008 to 0.025 in the other six domains). The banked pairs show the same thing. Recall gaps are -0.255 for customer_support to devops (interval [-0.347, -0.161]), -0.255 for saas_admin to devops, then -0.240, -0.213, -0.213, and -0.200, so six pairs fall below the preregistered -0.10 floor. Three pairs into saas_admin have gaps of +0.427. Both documents use the false premise to discount a supported confirmatory outcome: H3.2 'held, but only because recall is near zero in every domain' (README) and 'gaps between domains are small by construction' (REPORT). That misreports the result.

blocking.title: Gate G7 can pass when E2 did not run as preregistered
blocking.evidence: g7 reads the prereg/0003 config but only compares its prevalences and budgets with constants. It never checks: the results' monitors and sets against config['monitors']; the interval method against config['headline']['method']; or whether the preregistered fixed-threshold, time-to-detection, breakdown, and size-ladder analyses exist for the preregistered monitors. Counterexample, run on a scratch clone of e403a4e: I deleted every estimate, breakdown, and ladder rung of the preregistered monitor model:qwen3-4b-q4_k_m from artifacts/e2/results.json and committed. ship_check.g7 then returned 'G7 PASS 8 monitors in 4 families, full grid, intervals present'. B1 is a live case: preregistered breakdowns are missing for two monitors and G7 passes. The make reproduce step in G10 only checks that results.json matches what the current tools/analyze.py produces, so an analysis that leaves out a preregistered monitor or analysis passes both gates.

blocking.title: Gate G8 can pass with null results unreported
blocking.evidence: g8 only checks the hypotheses that the results file happens to list. It never compares them with the preregistered set: prereg/0004 hypotheses H3.1, H3.2, and H3.3 per monitor and target prevalence; prereg/0005 H4.1 and H4.2 per pair. Counterexample, run on a scratch clone of e403a4e: I removed the two not_supported H3.1 entries from artifacts/e3/results.json and committed. ship_check.g8 then returned 'G8 PASS E3 6 hypotheses (0 null or inconclusive); E4 8 hypotheses (0 null or inconclusive) reported'. So the gate whose property is 'reported, including null results' passes after the null results are deleted. An analysis that never emits a hypothesis would pass both G8 and the reproduce step of G10.

non_blocking.title: FPR at the budget is banked and printed far tighter than the benign runs can certify. Examples: primary, 1e-4, 5/10k gives 0.000500 [0.000499, 0.000500] from 2,373 runs, where 3/n is 0.00126; dataset, 1e-3, 20/10k gives [0.00100, 0.00157] from 8 clusters. The README quickstart's baserate eval prints 'no false-positive rate below 0.312 can be certified' and then 'FPR [95%] 0.00191 [0.0019, 0.00196]'. Label it as fixed by the budget or drop the interval.

The three Armour rule configurations score every primary trace identically, and every full-set trace except 9 to 18 Armour records. README and REPORT present them as three monitors without saying so, and the size ladder's 'best rule monitor' is a tie broken by list order.

Dataset-set estimates (8 benign and 7 violation clusters) are marked e0_supported because the closest-design rule maps them to the 2,000-cluster E0 design. No E0 design validates intervals with so few clusters, yet README quotes 0.930 [0.436, 1.000] and 1.000 [0.535, 1.000] with no caveat about this.

'Every interval was checked by preregistered simulation' overstates E0. E0 covers the budget-recall and fixed-threshold methods only. It does not cover the E3 percentile, E4 holdout-bootstrap, time-to-detection, or label-audit intervals.

The 50 'no valid call of the drawn type' false-completion skips are blamed on the subject model. In fact runner.py raises that skip before the model is consulted, when finishing as complete at the drawn step would not be a false completion.
The E4 key-result heading 'beat the expensive monitor alone' is contradicted by pair p4 (cascade test recall 0.002 against 0.004 for the 8B alone), which the prose never mentions.
The preregistered crossing rule did produce an answer: crossing rung 8B, not clear (size_ladder.crossing_rung). REPORT instead says 'the preregistered crossing question has no answer'.

'Deviations from the preregistrations. Three' leaves out smaller undeclared analysis choices: H3.3 intervals widened to include the point estimate (tools/analyze.py:718), the tie-weighted time-to-detection expectation, E4 leaving out cached records (none existed), and the D23 and D24 readings.

E4 n_train_runs and n_test_runs add benign and violation clusters together, so a source run behind both an inserted violation and its benign trace counts twice (n_test_runs 1710 against 1400 independent). This is the same defect that d4f6f42 fixed for E2.

The E2 primary, E3, and E4 bootstraps resample benign and violation clusters independently, although 618 inserted violations share a source run with a benign trace. E0 did not simulate this cross-class dependence, so 'resample or count whole source runs' overstates what is done.

E0 support for the composite method comes from n2000_p100 (100 violations) and is applied to E2's 1,045 violations, where the Clopper-Pearson part narrows and the benign-tail bootstrap carries more of the interval. binormal_d3 at 5/10k already shows coverage of 0.674. State this as a threat to validity.

G6 recomputes agreement only from the audit items' own fields. It does not check the items against the corpus labels or the preregistered sample. I checked both by hand: the sample reproduces from seed 1104 and there are 0 mismatches.

Inserted calls carry fixed template values (for example forms.fill 'name=Test User; team=platform'), which a monitor or auditor could use as a tell. Agreement on inserted violations in the audit was 60 of 60. Note this under limitations.
Only transcript hashes are banked for the label audit, not the instructions given to the auditor agents, so the blindness claim rests partly on text that is not banked.
The E2 cascade's escalation threshold tau is fixed from the full sample and is not re-estimated in the bootstrap, so the cascade interval leaves out escalation-threshold uncertainty.
Stale state lines: CORRECTIONS.md still opens with 'No corrections yet' above three entries, and STATUS.md says 'Updated 2026-11-05' over content from 2026-11-11.
The quickstart is labeled offline, but it begins with git clone and make setup (uv sync), which need the network on a fresh machine.
The abstract says the corpus, scores, and analyses 'are released with the code', but the repository is private and nothing has been published.
Commit trailers name the session model, although CLAUDE.md says commit messages never do. DECISIONS.md D13 records Raj's request to keep the trailers, so reconcile the two.
